label: Mongolian horse

names.text: Alternate names as given in the research input. The fetched article text did not list them, so the page does not confirm them; 'Mongolian horse' is the article title.

about.text: The native horse of Mongolia and northern China (Inner Mongolia). In summer its mares are milked six times a day, and the milk is made into airag and kumis.

sources.text: Article text: mares milked six times a day in summer (once every two hours); milk becomes airag and kumis; country of origin Mongolia and northern China (Inner Mongolia).

Country of origin given as Mongolia and northern China (Inner Mongolia). The article gives no formation dates; it says the breed is largely unchanged since Genghis Khan's time, which is not a date range and is not used here.

The article gives 0.11 lb of milk per milking and a yearly production of 662 lb, citing Cheng 1984 (FAO). 662 lb converted to kg is about 300 kg; the conversion is mine, not the source's. Year is that of the cited source. Lactation length and the place of the measurement are not given.
Dairy: the milk becomes airag and kumis. Riding: the article says nomads of the central Asian steppes are documented as riding horses from 2000 BC.

facts.v: In winter 2009 to 2010, 188,270 Mongol horses died.
Kept outdoors in temperatures from 30 °C in summer to −40 °C in winter, losing about 30% of body weight in winter and early spring.

sources.text: Article text: temperature range 30 °C (86 °F) in summer to −40 °C in winter; winter and early spring weight loss about 30% of body weight. No year given.

gaps: Current population and its year, the DAD-IS risk status, lactation length and milk composition were not found in the article. A 2021 Journal of Equine Science study of grazing Mongolian mares (doi 10.1294/jes.32.91) turned up in search, but its full text could not be opened (the page showed only the abstract), so its figures are not used.
